page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. The instance delivers 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 256.0 GB, establishing a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, operating with 133 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional multi-threaded computational efficiency and memory throughput. The server lands in the top decile for multi-core evaluations, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,794.0 and a Clang software compilation score of 81,827.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 480.23 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 236.01 GB/sec on writes. Furthermore, static web serving throughput measures 114.48 GB/sec, alongside 132.0 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-core CPU metrics remain in the middle quartile, as seen in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench baseline results.

Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the high core count and dedicated physical core architecture, which eliminates thread contention common in hyperthreaded systems while providing significant memory throughput per resource unit. Tradeoffs include the lack of ephemeral local storage, requiring network-attached storage configurations, and moderate per-thread performance relative to its strong multi-core scaling. The instance is suited for multi-threaded build systems, containerized microservice clusters, distributed in-memory data stores, and high-throughput network serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors built on the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 64 dedicated physical arm64 cores running at 2.8 GHz without multithreading, coupled with 256.0 GB of system memory to maintain a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not provided, and no discrete GPUs are present, with network performance supported by a 133 Gbps baseline capacity. Benchmarks reveal top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 480.23 GB/sec on large reads, alongside standout multi-core execution in software compilation and Redis caching throughput reaching 132.0 million operations per second. While single-threaded processing performs within the median range, the full physical core allocation ensures predictable thread isolation. The instance is best suited for concurrent enterprise applications, high-volume web serving, large-scale Redis caching, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
